chambersData.b7:
DeForest's labor & Employment practice advises employers whose workforce stability is fundamental to business continuity. Acting as strategic counsel to multinational and domestic companies, the team combines labor advisory, litigation, collective labor relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance into a fully integrated national platform capable of supporting complex operations throughout Mexico.
Rather than approaching labor law as a reactive discipline, the practice helps employers anticipate labor risk, strengthen governance frameworks and preserve operational continuity throughout the entire employment lifecycle—from hiring and day-to-day advisory to collective bargaining, workforce restructurings, regulatory inspections, social security matters and high-value litigation.
The practice has developed particular strength advising companies operating in highly regulated and labor-intensive industries, including automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, retail, technology, telecommunications and financial services, where employment strategy directly affects production continuity, investment certainty and long-term business performance.
The department is led by one of the country's most experienced labor teams. Eduardo Garduño has become one of Mexico's leading labor strategists for multinational employers, combining more than two decades of experience advising major corporations with senior public-sector insight that enables him to translate complex regulatory environments into practical business solutions.
Jaime Bustamante contributes the perspective of one of the region's largest employers, having previously served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central and South America at ManpowerGroup, where he oversaw workforce structures across multiple jurisdictions.
Raymundo Carreño brings the institutional knowledge accumulated during nearly four decades as General Legal Director of Volkswagen de México, offering clients strategic judgement developed through some of the country's most significant labor negotiations and organisational transformations.
The leadership team is further strengthened by Javier Atzin Vallejo, whose practice focuses on labor compliance, social security and workforce integration; Edgar Barreto, recognised for his experience in labor litigation and IMSS matters; Andrés Cabrera, who leads the firm's labor practice across the Bajío region; Erick Pérez, a specialist in complex litigation and constitutional proceedings; and José Alberto Díaz, whose practice combines labor, social security and administrative litigation in highly regulated industries.
Today the practice advises employers whose combined workforce exceeds one million employees throughout Mexico. Its work extends well beyond litigation management and encompasses nationwide litigation portfolios involving hundreds of simultaneous proceedings, including approximately 700 labor disputes managed by the firm's Puebla team. The practice also advises on collective bargaining negotiations, union representation disputes, labor integration following mergers and acquisitions, employer restructurings, labor and social security audits, constitutional litigation, preventive governance programmes and regulatory inspections before the Ministry of Labor, IMSS and INFONAVIT.
Clients consistently retain DeForest not simply to resolve labor disputes, but to preserve organisational stability in environments where workforce disruption could directly affect production, investment and corporate reputation. This preventive, business-oriented philosophy has positioned the practice among Mexico's leading advisers to multinational employers navigating increasingly sophisticated labor challenges.
During the last twelve months alone, the team has also assisted more than twenty clients in connection with labor inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and has handled numerous audits involving labor and social security compliance, reinforcing its position as trusted counsel for employers operating in highly regulated sectors.
The firm's sustained growth is reflected in its recognition by Chambers Latin America 2025 for General Business Law (Querétaro), The Legal 500 since 2024 for labor & Employment and IFLR1000 2025 for Corporate & M&A, confirming the continued consolidation of DeForest as one of Mexico's most sophisticated full-service business law firms.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 1
matters.title: Confidential Matter 1
matters.summary:
Mextypsa, one of Mexico's leading engineering and infrastructure companies, relies on DeForest as its strategic labor counsel for projects where workforce governance is fundamental to successful execution. The firm's mandate extends beyond day-to-day employment advice, encompassing the design of labor structures capable of supporting large-scale infrastructure projects while preserving regulatory compliance and operational continuity throughout each project's lifecycle.

One of the most significant engagements involved the Guadalajara Metro Line 4 Project, a USD 552 million infrastructure development requiring a sophisticated labor framework to manage project-based recruitment, documentation, workforce administration and eventual demobilisation under intense public scrutiny. Simultaneously, DeForest represented the client in complex litigation arising from the Coahuila Wind Farm Project, where an adverse labor judgment threatened liabilities exceeding MXN 5.5 million.

Rather than treating these matters as isolated engagements, DeForest developed a comprehensive labor governance strategy combining preventive advisory with high-stakes dispute resolution. The team designed the contractual and compliance architecture supporting the Guadalajara Metro project, supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies and successfully challenged the adverse labor judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the client's procedural rights and reopening the litigation.

Today, the firm manages more than twenty labor disputes for Mextypsa representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million. Through early negotiation strategies and disciplined litigation management, DeForest has consistently reduced financial exposure while protecting operational continuity across the client's infrastructure portfolio.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 2
matters.title: Confidential Matter 2
matters.summary:
Bonatti has entrusted DeForest with the labor governance strategy supporting several of Mexico's largest energy infrastructure projects, where uninterrupted workforce stability is essential to the successful execution of multi-billion-dollar developments. Acting as strategic labor counsel, the firm advises throughout the entire project lifecycle, integrating labor compliance, collective employment matters and litigation strategy into a single governance framework.

The mandate includes the Energía Mayakan Pipeline Expansion, valued at more than USD 2 billion, the Cuxtal II expansion, the Ojinaga-El Encino Gas Pipeline and strategic operational support for ENI México's energy projects in Tabasco.

DeForest designed and implemented the labor architecture supporting each project, including workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute prevention strategies and workforce demobilisation. Alongside this preventive work, the firm managed more than twenty labor disputes arising during project execution, resolving the overwhelming majority through conciliation and reducing potential financial exposure by approximately eighty percent.

The team also prevented an imminent strike that threatened to halt operations linked to Mexico's strategic energy infrastructure, safeguarding contractual performance, operational continuity and the client's long-term commercial position. Today, DeForest acts not simply as litigation counsel but as a long-term strategic partner supporting some of the country's most critical infrastructure developments.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 3
matters.title: Confidential Matter 3
matters.summary:
Following Schaeffler's global acquisition of Vitesco Technologies, DeForest was appointed to lead one of the most significant post-acquisition labor integration projects currently underway in Mexico. The transaction required the harmonisation of employment structures across multiple manufacturing facilities while ensuring uninterrupted operations throughout the integration process.

The firm designed and implemented the labor integration strategy affecting facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labor governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.

Parallel to the integration, DeForest manages thirty-five active labor proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, ensuring that litigation strategy remains fully aligned with the client's unified post-acquisition governance model. Through this combination of workforce integration, compliance and litigation management, the firm has become a long-term strategic adviser supporting one of the world's leading automotive suppliers.

matters.title: Confidential Matter 4
matters.client: GeNI de México, S.A de C.V.
matters.summary:
GeNI de México, a strategic supplier to Volkswagen, Audi, Ford and General Motors, engaged DeForest during one of the most sensitive moments in its labor relations. A deteriorating relationship with the union had created an imminent strike risk capable of disrupting production across multiple automotive supply chains.

DeForest led the collective bargaining negotiations, rebuilding dialogue between management and union representatives while designing a renewed agreement that balanced operational efficiency with employee expectations. Beyond preventing the strike, the negotiated framework introduced process improvements and operational efficiencies while preserving uninterrupted production for several of the world's leading automotive manufacturers.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to transform high-risk labor disputes into long-term governance solutions that strengthen workforce stability while protecting business continuity throughout the automotive sector.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 5
matters.title: Confidential Matter 5
matters.summary:
Nueva Empresa, S.C. engaged DeForest in two high-value wrongful termination proceedings that raised issues extending well beyond financial exposure. Following procedural objections concerning the legal standing of the company's attorney-in-fact, the labor court refused to recognise the company's representation, disregarded its defence and issued an adverse ruling despite the existence of valid notarial documentation confirming the attorney's legal identity.

The dispute presented a significant constitutional question concerning due process, legal certainty and the recognition of legally valid identity changes, creating an important opportunity to clarify procedural standards within Mexico's labor justice system.

DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

Beyond the financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million, the matter is significant for reinforcing constitutional protections governing procedural fairness and the legal recognition of identity, establishing an important precedent with broader implications for labor litigation in Mexico.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 6
matters.title: Confidential Matter 6
matters.summary:
Brose México entrusted DeForest with the management of a highly sensitive collective labor dispute involving the ownership of the collective bargaining agreement at one of its manufacturing facilities in Querétaro. The proceedings formed part of the broader transformation of Mexico's collective labor relations framework, where union representation challenges increasingly affect business continuity for major industrial employers.

DeForest designed and implemented the client's negotiation and litigation strategy, guiding the company through complex union representation proceedings while preserving uninterrupted operations. Through proactive dialogue and careful procedural management, the firm successfully prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response labor Mechanism, protecting both operational continuity and the client's long-term industrial stability.

The matter demonstrates DeForest's ability to navigate one of the most challenging aspects of Mexico's post-reform labor landscape, combining collective bargaining expertise with strategic business risk management.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 7
matters.title: Confidential Matter 7
matters.summary:
One of Mexico's most extraordinary labor disputes gave rise to this engagement. A former senior executive obtained a labor judgment exceeding MXN 2.162 billion, exposing Enerflex and indirectly PEMEX to unprecedented financial and governance risks. Against this exceptional backdrop, the employee retained DeForest to develop an alternative strategy capable of unlocking negotiations that had reached complete deadlock.

Rather than relying exclusively on litigation, DeForest designed a parallel mediation strategy running alongside the judicial proceedings. The firm established common valuation criteria, governance-based negotiation parameters and structured settlement mechanisms capable of facilitating constructive dialogue between parties that had previously been unwilling to negotiate.

The strategy ultimately generated a series of favourable settlement agreements that preserved the employee's legitimate interests while significantly reducing systemic exposure for Enerflex and preventing PEMEX from facing joint liability arising from one of the largest labor awards ever issued in Mexico. The matter remains ongoing, with DeForest continuing to coordinate negotiations alongside PEMEX's in-house legal team.

This engagement reflects the firm's ability to resolve disputes where legal complexity, commercial interests and public-sector exposure intersect at the highest level.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 9
matters.title: Confidential Matter 9
matters.summary:
Securitas de México operates one of the country's largest private security workforces, a sector characterised by high employee turnover, geographically dispersed personnel and constant regulatory exposure. Maintaining consistent labor governance across multiple locations presents significant operational challenges, particularly in an industry where workforce management directly affects service delivery and contractual performance.

As the company expanded its operations across Puebla, Mexico City, Torreón and Veracruz, it entrusted DeForest with the strategic management of its labor litigation portfolio while strengthening preventive employment practices capable of supporting long-term operational stability.

DeForest currently manages more than fifty labor proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 10 million while simultaneously advising the client on documentation, employment governance and risk mitigation across its expanding national footprint. Rather than addressing disputes individually, the firm has implemented a coordinated labor strategy that combines litigation management with preventive advisory, enabling the client to maintain consistent employment standards across multiple jurisdictions.

The engagement demonstrates DeForest's ability to provide scalable labor governance solutions for employers operating large, decentralised workforces in highly regulated industries.

American Axle & Manufacturing, one of the world's leading automotive component manufacturers, appointed DeForest as its strategic labor counsel for its Mexican operations in early 2026. Beyond the immediate advisory work, the mandate positions DeForest as long-term strategic labor counsel for one of the automotive industry's most significant global manufacturers operating in Mexico.

matters.summary:
BADAK, a technology consultancy specialising in software development, entrusted DeForest with the defence of several high-exposure employment disputes that threatened to generate disproportionate financial and operational consequences for a growing technology business. Beyond the immediate litigation, the client required a strategy capable of containing escalating liabilities while preserving commercial stability.

The matters included multiple wrongful termination claims with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 1.5 million, one of which had already escalated to approximately MXN 1.06 million by the time constitutional relief became available.

DeForest combined constitutional litigation, procedural strategy and commercial negotiation to fundamentally reshape the client's litigation position. Through disciplined sequencing of legal actions and settlement discussions, the firm reduced one of the principal claims from approximately MXN 1.06 million to MXN 20,000, representing a reduction of approximately 98% while continuing to manage the remaining proceedings.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to contain significant employment liabilities through sophisticated litigation strategy while preserving business continuity for rapidly growing technology companies.

Volkswagen de México, one of the country's largest industrial employers, together with Volkswagen Financial Services, continues to rely on DeForest to support the labor governance of its Mexican operations. The engagement spans complex employment matters affecting one of the most sophisticated manufacturing environments in the country, where regulatory certainty and workforce stability are fundamental to uninterrupted production.

DeForest manages active labor proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 280 million while simultaneously advising on employment agreements, internal workplace regulations, disciplinary procedures, corporate powers of attorney and broader workforce governance initiatives across the client's operations in Puebla. Rather than treating litigation and advisory work separately, the firm provides an integrated governance model that combines dispute management with preventive labor strategy.

The long-standing relationship reflects the confidence placed in DeForest to support one of Mexico's most significant industrial employers through an increasingly complex labor and regulatory environment.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 16
matters.title: Confidential Matter 16
matters.summary:
Robert Bosch de México operates one of the country's largest industrial workforces, employing approximately 17,000 people across multiple business divisions. Maintaining consistent labor governance within an organisation of this scale requires sophisticated employment structures capable of supporting operational efficiency while ensuring full regulatory compliance.

DeForest advises the client on the design and implementation of employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labor governance policies and union-related matters, while also leading employer registration processes for Bosch Rexroth and coordinating social security structures across the organisation.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to build and maintain labor governance platforms supporting complex industrial operations where workforce management directly influences operational continuity and long-term business performance.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 17
matters.title: Confidential Matter 17
matters.summary:
Coats de México engaged DeForest to support a significant workforce transformation affecting multiple manufacturing facilities across Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. The mandate required not only the redesign of the client's employment framework but also the careful management of sensitive collective labor issues capable of affecting manufacturing continuity.

The firm developed the client's labor architecture from the ground up, including employment agreements, labor policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce governance protocols. Simultaneously, DeForest negotiated union-related matters involving exposure exceeding MXN 12.5 million while leading collective bargaining discussions that enabled the client to preserve operational stability throughout the restructuring process.

The engagement highlights the firm's ability to combine workforce transformation with sophisticated collective labor negotiations for major industrial employers.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 18
matters.title: Confidential Matter 18
matters.summary:
REGSA entrusted DeForest with the design of its labor governance framework as the company strengthened its industrial operations. Alongside the implementation of core employment structures, the client required strategic support in navigating Mexico's increasingly complex union representation regime.

DeForest designed the client's employment documentation, labor policies and collective bargaining framework while simultaneously leading union representativeness proceedings requiring precise procedural strategy and continuous engagement with labor authorities.

By integrating preventive labor governance with sophisticated collective labor representation, the firm has enabled the client to strengthen organisational stability while navigating one of the most challenging aspects of Mexico's post-reform labor environment.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 19
matters.title: Confidential Matter 19
matters.summary:
Omron, a global leader in industrial automation and advanced manufacturing technologies, engaged DeForest to modernise its labor governance framework following the implementation of significant employment reforms in Mexico. The mandate focused on ensuring that the client's employment structures remained aligned with evolving regulatory obligations while supporting the operational flexibility required by a sophisticated manufacturing business.

The engagement required a comprehensive review of remote-work policies, employment documentation, labor compliance procedures and social security obligations within a rapidly changing regulatory environment.

DeForest redesigned the client's employment documentation, updated internal labor policies and implemented governance mechanisms supporting hybrid working arrangements, IMSS compliance and ongoing labor reform obligations. The firm also delivered practical guidance to management teams, enabling consistent implementation of the revised framework across the organisation.

Rather than responding to isolated compliance issues, DeForest developed a preventive governance model designed to minimise regulatory exposure while preserving the operational agility required by a global industrial business.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 20
matters.title: Confidential Matter 20
matters.summary:
Benteler, one of the world's leading automotive suppliers, entrusted DeForest with one of the most sensitive labor challenges currently affecting industrial employers in Mexico: a union representativeness dispute capable of disrupting operations at one of its manufacturing facilities in Puebla. The matter arose within the broader transformation of Mexico's collective labor framework, where representation challenges increasingly influence business continuity across the automotive sector.

DeForest assumed responsibility for the client's strategic response, combining litigation, collective bargaining strategy and continuous negotiations with the competing unions. The firm's objective extended beyond resolving the legal dispute; it focused on preserving operational stability while ensuring full compliance with Mexico's labor legislation and respect for employees' collective rights.

Alongside the representation proceedings, DeForest continues strengthening the client's labor governance platform through the implementation of employment agreements, internal labor policies and collective bargaining documentation, reinforcing long-term organisational stability.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 21
matters.title: Confidential Matter 21
matters.summary:
Grupo Radio Centro engaged DeForest to manage a highly sensitive internal employment investigation involving allegations against a senior executive. Beyond the immediate employment implications, the matter carried significant reputational risk for one of Mexico's best-known media organisations, requiring a careful balance between procedural integrity, confidentiality and organisational stability.

DeForest designed and supervised the internal investigation, coordinating evidence-gathering, legal analysis and strategic decision-making while ensuring compliance with applicable employment standards. Through an objective and carefully structured process, the firm prevented litigation valued at approximately MXN 750,000 while protecting the client's reputation during a particularly sensitive period.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to manage complex workplace investigations where legal, commercial and reputational considerations converge.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 22
matters.title: Confidential Matter 22
matters.summary:
Cinemex, one of Mexico's largest cinema operators with more than 11,000 employees nationwide, relies on DeForest to manage one of the country's most significant labor litigation portfolios following the operational disruption generated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The client's nationwide footprint requires a unified legal strategy capable of maintaining consistency across multiple jurisdictions operating under evolving labor reform criteria.

DeForest coordinates a nationwide litigation platform comprising approximately two hundred active labor proceedings with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 60.5 million. Beyond litigation management, the team leads conciliation proceedings, advises on workforce restructurings, strengthens employment documentation and continuously refines preventive governance measures designed to reduce future labor contingencies.

By combining centralised litigation management with preventive advisory, the firm enables the client to maintain operational stability while reducing systemic employment risk across one of Mexico's largest consumer-facing workforces.

matters.summary:
Art Human, a financial services company active in real estate financing and executive search, relies on DeForest as external labor counsel for the management of its employment platform. Beyond active litigation, the client sought to strengthen internal governance while preparing the organisation for increasingly demanding labor and social security inspections.

DeForest manages the client's labor litigation portfolio while simultaneously conducting audits, strengthening internal controls, harmonising employment procedures and implementing preventive governance measures. The effectiveness of this approach was demonstrated when three separate inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and IMSS concluded without the imposition of any fines, despite combined potential exposure approaching MXN 2 million.

The engagement demonstrates how preventive labor governance can substantially reduce regulatory exposure while supporting sustainable organisational growth.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 24
matters.title: Confidential Matter 24
matters.summary:
SKF Industrial, a global technology company specialising in bearings, seals and industrial engineering solutions, engaged DeForest to strengthen the legal framework supporting an operation of approximately 200 employees in Mexico. As a highly technical manufacturing business, the client required an employment structure capable of supporting operational discipline, regulatory compliance and consistent workforce governance across its industrial activities.

DeForest conducted a comprehensive review of the client's labor framework, redesigning internal workplace regulations, employment agreements, mixed commissions and labor policies to ensure full alignment with current Mexican labor legislation and the client's global governance standards.
Beyond updating documentation, the engagement established a preventive employment platform designed to reduce regulatory exposure, strengthen day-to-day workforce management and provide a legally robust framework capable of supporting the client's long-term industrial operations in Mexico.

The integrated nature of the mandate allows the client to address employment and corporate matters under a unified legal strategy while strengthening the stability and scalability of its manufacturing platform.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to provide multidisciplinary legal support for growing industrial businesses requiring coordinated labor and corporate advice.

matters.title: Confidential Matter 26
matters.summary:
Shirushi, a regional restaurant group operating approximately twenty locations, engaged DeForest to support the labor governance of a business operating within one of the most labor-intensive sectors of the Mexican economy. High employee turnover, decentralised operations and the operational demands of the hospitality industry required a practical employment framework capable of supporting consistent workforce management across multiple sites.

DeForest advises the client across the full spectrum of labor matters, including employment documentation, workforce policies, disciplinary procedures and day-to-day employment advisory. The firm has implemented a preventive governance model designed to standardise employment practices across all restaurant locations while reducing litigation risk and strengthening regulatory compliance.

The engagement illustrates DeForest's ability to adapt sophisticated labor governance principles to operational environments characterised by high workforce mobility and continuous business activity.

Natividad Abogados, one of Mexico's leading specialist labor law firms, appointed DeForest as its regional correspondent counsel for labor litigation in central Mexico. The mandate reflects the confidence placed by a recognised market leader in DeForest's ability to represent clients in complex employment proceedings outside its principal jurisdiction.

DeForest manages approximately forty-five labor proceedings on behalf of Natividad Abogados, coordinating local litigation strategy, procedural management and court representation while ensuring consistency with the client's national legal approach.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's technical credibility within the legal market itself, acting as trusted regional counsel for one of Mexico's best-known labor law practices.

The engagement highlights the firm's ability to manage geographically dispersed workforces through integrated labor governance and sophisticated collective labor strategy.

SEBNMX, an automotive manufacturer employing approximately 2,000 people in Tlaxcala, engaged DeForest to modernise the legal framework supporting one of its principal manufacturing operations. The mandate arose within the context of Mexico's labor reform, requiring the client to strengthen its employment governance while maintaining uninterrupted industrial operations.

DeForest conducted a comprehensive review of the client's labor governance platform, updating internal workplace regulations, employment agreements, labor policies and mixed commissions while supporting the implementation of the latest labor reform requirements. The engagement focused on ensuring that the client's employment framework remained operationally effective, legally compliant and capable of supporting a large industrial workforce.

By integrating legal compliance with practical workforce governance, the firm strengthened the client's long-term organisational resilience while reducing regulatory exposure.

matters.name: Matter 31
matters.title: Matter 31
matters.summary:
SCOTCH engaged DeForest to review and restructure its corporate and labor framework following the introduction of Mexico's specialised services regime (REPSE). The matter required a multidisciplinary approach combining labor, corporate and regulatory expertise to ensure that the client's business model remained fully aligned with the country's evolving outsourcing framework.

Working jointly across its corporate and labor practices, DeForest carried out a comprehensive review of the client's corporate structure, specialised services model, bylaws and REPSE registration while simultaneously conducting an audit of more than eighty suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised services agreements.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to advise clients on complex regulatory transformations where employment, corporate governance and commercial operations converge.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 32
matters.title: Confidential Matter 32
matters.summary:
Grupo Solana, a diversified automotive and real estate group employing more than 1,200 people, retained DeForest to implement a complex employer substitution process affecting its workforce structure. The matter required careful coordination between labor and regulatory authorities to ensure business continuity while restructuring the group's employment platform.

DeForest designed and executed the legal strategy necessary to reactivate the employer registration that had previously been cancelled, allowing the employer substitution process to proceed without disrupting the client's operations. The firm coordinated the labor transition while ensuring full compliance with applicable employment regulations and preserving workforce stability throughout the restructuring.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to support complex corporate reorganisations where labor law plays a critical role in enabling business transformation.

analysis.summary: Veredicto ejecutivo: presentar una candidatura de primera inclusión en Chambers Latin America: Labour & Employment — Mexico; no procede hablar de subida de bandas. La comprobación oficial acotada no halló una coincidencia exacta de DeForest en la tabla de Labour & Employment México, sin acreditar ausencia de reconocimiento en otros alcances ni permitir prever una banda. La propuesta muestra una práctica employer-side coherente en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas, prevención de paros, litigación de cartera, reestructuraciones, cumplimiento laboral y seguridad social. SCHAEFFLER es el hero: frente a Volkswagen, que acredita cartera y gobernanza continuada, combina una integración definida tras adquisición, armonización laboral y colectiva en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, 35 procedimientos activos y liderazgo atribuido a Eduardo Garduño. Tres perfiles oficiales recuperados de Band 5 muestran como contexto capacidades de negociación colectiva, litigios individuales y colectivos, seguridad social y asesoría no contenciosa, pero no aportan calibración completa ni posición comparativa. La vulnerabilidad pendiente es confirmar una sola vez que los asuntos seleccionados reflejan actividad relevante en la ventana de investigación; la evidencia individual se concentra en Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez.

chambersData.enhanced_b7:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on workforce stability, collective labour relations, employment litigation, labour and social-security compliance, inspections and workforce governance across Mexico. The team combines contentious and non-contentious work for employers operating in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including manufacturing, automotive, energy, infrastructure, technology, consumer services and financial services.

The practice is particularly active where employment strategy is closely connected to operational continuity. Its work includes post-acquisition labour integration, collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, prevention of work stoppages, nationwide labour litigation portfolios, workforce restructurings, employer substitutions, specialised-services compliance, internal investigations, employment documentation and social-security matters.

The team has advised on the harmonisation of labour structures for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees across six Mexican states following an acquisition; collective labour disputes involving union representation and strike risk; nationwide litigation platforms comprising approximately 200 active proceedings; and employment-governance projects for industrial workforces of up to approximately 17,000 employees. It also advises on labour-reform implementation, REPSE-related reviews and supplier audits, labour and social-security inspections, and constitutional labour litigation.

Eduardo Garduño leads the practice, with Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante, José Alberto Díaz Méndez and other members of the team contributing across collective labour, workforce governance, litigation, compliance and social-security mandates. The practice is positioned to support employers throughout the employment lifecycle, from preventive governance and documentation to high-risk collective disputes and complex contentious matters.

chambersData.original_b10:
DeForest's labor & Employment practice advises employers whose workforce stability is fundamental to business continuity. Acting as strategic counsel to multinational and domestic companies, the team combines labor advisory, litigation, collective labor relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance into a fully integrated national platform capable of supporting complex operations throughout Mexico.
Rather than approaching labor law as a reactive discipline, the practice helps employers anticipate labor risk, strengthen governance frameworks and preserve operational continuity throughout the entire employment lifecycle—from hiring and day-to-day advisory to collective bargaining, workforce restructurings, regulatory inspections, social security matters and high-value litigation.
The practice has developed particular strength advising companies operating in highly regulated and labor-intensive industries, including automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, retail, technology, telecommunications and financial services, where employment strategy directly affects production continuity, investment certainty and long-term business performance.
The department is led by one of the country's most experienced labor teams. Eduardo Garduño has become one of Mexico's leading labor strategists for multinational employers, combining more than two decades of experience advising major corporations with senior public-sector insight that enables him to translate complex regulatory environments into practical business solutions.
Jaime Bustamante contributes the perspective of one of the region's largest employers, having previously served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central and South America at ManpowerGroup, where he oversaw workforce structures across multiple jurisdictions.
Raymundo Carreño brings the institutional knowledge accumulated during nearly four decades as General Legal Director of Volkswagen de México, offering clients strategic judgement developed through some of the country's most significant labor negotiations and organisational transformations.
The leadership team is further strengthened by Javier Atzin Vallejo, whose practice focuses on labor compliance, social security and workforce integration; Edgar Barreto, recognised for his experience in labor litigation and IMSS matters; Andrés Cabrera, who leads the firm's labor practice across the Bajío region; Erick Pérez, a specialist in complex litigation and constitutional proceedings; and José Alberto Díaz, whose practice combines labor, social security and administrative litigation in highly regulated industries.
Today the practice advises employers whose combined workforce exceeds one million employees throughout Mexico. Its work extends well beyond litigation management and encompasses nationwide litigation portfolios involving hundreds of simultaneous proceedings, including approximately 700 labor disputes managed by the firm's Puebla team. The practice also advises on collective bargaining negotiations, union representation disputes, labor integration following mergers and acquisitions, employer restructurings, labor and social security audits, constitutional litigation, preventive governance programmes and regulatory inspections before the Ministry of Labor, IMSS and INFONAVIT.
Clients consistently retain DeForest not simply to resolve labor disputes, but to preserve organisational stability in environments where workforce disruption could directly affect production, investment and corporate reputation. This preventive, business-oriented philosophy has positioned the practice among Mexico's leading advisers to multinational employers navigating increasingly sophisticated labor challenges.
During the last twelve months alone, the team has also assisted more than twenty clients in connection with labor inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and has handled numerous audits involving labor and social security compliance, reinforcing its position as trusted counsel for employers operating in highly regulated sectors.
The firm's sustained growth is reflected in its recognition by Chambers Latin America 2025 for General Business Law (Querétaro), The Legal 500 since 2024 for labor & Employment and IFLR1000 2025 for Corporate & M&A, confirming the continued consolidation of DeForest as one of Mexico's most sophisticated full-service business law firms.

letter.portfolio: Cartera recomendada, en orden estratégico: 1. SCHAEFFLER — hero: Eduardo Garduño lideró la integración post-adquisición de más de 5.000 empleados en seis estados, con armonización de contratos, convenios colectivos, reglamentos, comisiones mixtas y políticas, y 35 procedimientos activos. 2. Brose México: Javier Atzin Vallejo dirigió estrategia de negociación y litigio en controversia de representatividad sindical; la fuente atribuye prevención de paros y de escalamiento bajo el Mecanismo Laboral de Respuesta Rápida del T-MEC. 3. GeNI de México: Eduardo Garduño y Carlos Rivera lideraron negociación colectiva ante huelga inminente; la fuente atribuye prevención de la huelga y continuidad productiva. 4. Volkswagen de México y VW Financial Services: Eduardo Garduño lidera procedimientos activos y asesoría sobre contratos, reglamentos, disciplina, poderes y gobernanza. 5. Cinemex: Eduardo Garduño y Fernanda Priego codirigen aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos, conciliaciones, reestructuraciones y prevención; Erick Pérez integra el equipo. 6. Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge: José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable de una reestructuración de aproximadamente ocho compañías, entidad de servicios especializados, sustituciones patronales, transición de plantilla y litigio de seguridad social. 7. Coats de México: Eduardo Garduño lidera transformación multisede, documentación laboral y colectiva y negociaciones sindicales que, según la fuente, preservaron estabilidad operativa. 8. Bonatti SpA / Bonatti México: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera arquitectura laboral, prevención de controversias y desmovilización para infraestructura energética; la fuente atribuye prevención de huelga inminente. 9. Benteler: Eduardo Garduño lidera respuesta a controversia de representatividad sindical mediante litigio, estrategia colectiva y negociación con sindicatos competidores. 10. Mextypsa: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera estructuración contractual y de cumplimiento, desmovilización y amparo que reabrió el litigio; persisten más de 20 controversias. 11. Nueva Empresa: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera amparo en el que un Tribunal Colegiado concedió protección, reconoció legitimación y restituyó defensa. 12. BADAK: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera litigio constitucional, estrategia procesal y negociación; la fuente informa reducción de aproximadamente MXN 1,06 millones a MXN 20.000. 13. Grupo Solana: José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable en sustitución patronal para más de 1.200 personas, con reactivación de registro patronal y transición sin interrupción. 14. SCOTCH: único asunto publicable; José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable de revisión REPSE, estructura corporativa y auditoría de más de 80 proveedores. 15. Robert Bosch de México: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera documentación, disciplina, asuntos sindicales, registros patronales y estructuras de seguridad social para aproximadamente 17.000 empleados. 16. Recicla Ambiente: Eduardo Garduño lidera asesoría laboral, negociación colectiva y sindical en seis localidades para aproximadamente 700 empleados. 17. SEBNMX: Eduardo Garduño lidera actualización de reglamentos, contratos, políticas y comisiones mixtas para aproximadamente 2.000 empleados. 18. REGSA: Eduardo Garduño lidera documentación laboral, negociación colectiva y representatividad sindical. 19. Art Human: Jaime Bustamante lidera cartera, auditorías y controles; tres inspecciones de STPS e IMSS concluyeron sin multas. 20. Grupo Radio Centro: Jaime Bustamante lidera investigación laboral interna sensible; la fuente atribuye prevención de litigio. Los importes de asuntos confidenciales, incluso si constan en la fuente, deben excluirse de prosa pública; los asuntos pendientes deben presentarse como trabajo en curso.
letter.leadership:
La limitación común: la búsqueda individual oficial acotada no encontró coincidencias exactas en la tabla de Chambers Labour & Employment México; no demuestra ausencia de reconocimiento en otras prácticas o ediciones. Las categorías son objetivos de candidatura, no reconocimientos establecidos ni previsiones.

Eduardo Garduño — candidato individual principal, objetivo Band 5. Es socio y concentra la atribución más amplia: lidera SCHAEFFLER, GeNI, Volkswagen, Coats, REGSA, SEBNMX y Recicla Ambiente, y codirige Cinemex. La candidatura debe centrarse en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas de alto riesgo, litigación de cartera y gobernanza industrial. El objetivo Band 5 se conserva por seniority y reiteración de liderazgo, sin afirmar ranking actual. Deben obtenerse referencias sobre liderazgo, negociación y servicio continuado.

Javier Atzin Vallejo — segundo candidato individual, objetivo Band 5. Es socio; por ello, la sugerencia previa de Associate to Watch se sustituyó correctamente por una candidatura de socio. Su prueba diferenciada comprende Brose, Bonatti, Mextypsa, Nueva Empresa, BADAK y Bosch. Debe posicionarse en relaciones colectivas, prevención de paros, litigación constitucional laboral, proyectos industriales y seguridad social. Faltan referencias y confirmación de actividad dentro de la ventana aplicable.

Jaime Bustamante — candidato de apoyo, objetivo Band 5. Es socio y lidera Art Human y Grupo Radio Centro, con evidencia de compliance preventivo, inspecciones, investigaciones internas y gestión de riesgo. Puede presentarse, pero su caso individual es menos fuerte en relaciones colectivas que los dos candidatos principales. Benteler y Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge no deben usarse como prueba de su liderazgo: las fuentes atribuyen esos mandatos a Eduardo Garduño y José Alberto Díaz Méndez, respectivamente. Requiere más referencias y mandatos core personalmente atribuidos.

José Alberto Díaz Méndez — candidato Associate to Watch. Su rol confirmado es Associate; debe describirse como associate lead o responsable, nunca como socio aunque el campo fuente diga “Lead Partner(s)”. Sus mandatos sustantivos son SCOTCH, Grupo Solana y Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge, además de participación de equipo en Volkswagen y Bosch. La categoría es congruente con trabajo en REPSE, sustitución patronal, transición de plantilla y seguridad social. Debe documentarse su función técnica concreta y obtener referencias de clientes.

Erick Pérez — desarrollar, sin candidatura formal. Es Associate y figura como integrante del equipo en Volkswagen, Cinemex y Benteler, pero no se le atribuyen dirección de audiencia, estrategia, negociación ni responsabilidad autónoma. Una eventual candidatura Associate to Watch exige roles personales repetidos y verificables.

Andrés Cabrera — desarrollar. Es Associate; la bio menciona trabajo contencioso, pero no hay asunto core atribuido. No procede candidatura hasta contar con dos o tres mandatos relevantes que identifiquen función, etapa procesal o resultado.

Raymundo Carreño — desarrollar. Es Associate. La experiencia previa puede reforzar su bio, pero no sustituye trabajo actual personalmente atribuido. No tiene mandatos core a su nombre; una candidatura Associate to Watch requiere evidencia contemporánea.

Edgar Barreto — desarrollar. Es Associate y su perfil es coherente con litigación laboral e IMSS, pero no hay mandatos core ni resultados atribuidos. Debe permanecer visible como integrante del equipo, sin candidatura individual en esta edición.

letter.evidence_gaps: Reservas y exclusiones comparativas: American Axle & Manufacturing queda en reserva por discrepancia entre “American Axle Manufactury” y “American Axle & Manufacturing”, inicio a comienzos de 2026 y falta de resultado final; no debe fijarse una variante como definitiva. TEKIA acredita estrategia de litigio y amparo, pero no resultado definitivo; queda detrás de Nueva Empresa, BADAK y Mextypsa, que aportan resultados procesales o cuantificados. Ramsa aporta auditorías, terminaciones sensibles y due diligence, pero se superpone con Art Human y SCOTCH; Grupo Radio Centro añade investigación interna y prevención de controversias. Securitas y Natividad Abogados muestran volumen, pero menos detalle jurídico que Cinemex, Volkswagen y los asuntos colectivos del núcleo. Omron, SKF, AUNDE, Sirushi/Shirushi, Corrugados y Empaques de Oriente y SEBNMX son asesoría o gobernanza útil, pero generalmente menos diferenciadora; en Sirushi/Shirushi persiste discrepancia de nombre. Enerflex es trabajo directo de controversias, pero el cliente fue el empleado y se reserva para mantener una narrativa employer-side. Grupo Dos describe una negociación exitosa, pero carece del detalle jurídico, procesal y cuantitativo de los asuntos seleccionados. La falta de fechas exactas o de estado formal no demuestra inelegibilidad; los asuntos con actividad narrativa pueden describirse como en curso, sin inferir fechas, cierres o resultados definitivos.
letter.executive_assessment: Veredicto ejecutivo: presentar una candidatura de primera inclusión en Chambers Latin America: Labour & Employment — Mexico; no procede hablar de subida de bandas. La comprobación oficial acotada no halló una coincidencia exacta de DeForest en la tabla de Labour & Employment México, sin acreditar ausencia de reconocimiento en otros alcances ni permitir prever una banda. La propuesta muestra una práctica employer-side coherente en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas, prevención de paros, litigación de cartera, reestructuraciones, cumplimiento laboral y seguridad social. SCHAEFFLER es el hero: frente a Volkswagen, que acredita cartera y gobernanza continuada, combina una integración definida tras adquisición, armonización laboral y colectiva en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, 35 procedimientos activos y liderazgo atribuido a Eduardo Garduño. Tres perfiles oficiales recuperados de Band 5 muestran como contexto capacidades de negociación colectiva, litigios individuales y colectivos, seguridad social y asesoría no contenciosa, pero no aportan calibración completa ni posición comparativa. La vulnerabilidad pendiente es confirmar una sola vez que los asuntos seleccionados reflejan actividad relevante en la ventana de investigación; la evidencia individual se concentra en Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez.

development.c2:
DeForest requests consideration for coverage in Labour & Employment in Mexico. The practice presents an employer-side offering that combines collective labour strategy, workforce integration, labour litigation, employment governance and labour and social-security compliance.

Representative work includes a post-acquisition labour integration affecting more than 5,000 employees across six states; collective labour mandates in which the team prevented work stoppages and addressed union-representation disputes; nationwide labour litigation management involving approximately 200 active proceedings; and workforce restructurings involving employer substitution, specialised-services structures and multi-company transitions. The team also handles inspections, internal employment investigations, constitutional labour litigation and preventive governance for industrial, infrastructure, consumer-facing and regulated businesses.

The practice’s leadership is demonstrated through named partners leading these mandates, while associates contribute to complex restructuring, REPSE and litigation work. This combination of collective labour capability, contentious experience and practical workforce-governance work supports appropriate Chambers coverage for the Mexico Labour & Employment market.
development.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on workforce stability, collective labour relations, employment litigation, labour and social-security compliance, inspections and workforce governance across Mexico. The team combines contentious and non-contentious work for employers operating in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including manufacturing, automotive, energy, infrastructure, technology, consumer services and financial services.

The practice is particularly active where employment strategy is closely connected to operational continuity. Its work includes post-acquisition labour integration, collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, prevention of work stoppages, nationwide labour litigation portfolios, workforce restructurings, employer substitutions, specialised-services compliance, internal investigations, employment documentation and social-security matters.

The team has advised on the harmonisation of labour structures for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees across six Mexican states following an acquisition; collective labour disputes involving union representation and strike risk; nationwide litigation platforms comprising approximately 200 active proceedings; and employment-governance projects for industrial workforces of up to approximately 17,000 employees. It also advises on labour-reform implementation, REPSE-related reviews and supplier audits, labour and social-security inspections, and constitutional labour litigation.

Eduardo Garduño leads the practice, with Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante, José Alberto Díaz Méndez and other members of the team contributing across collective labour, workforce governance, litigation, compliance and social-security mandates. The practice is positioned to support employers throughout the employment lifecycle, from preventive governance and documentation to high-risk collective disputes and complex contentious matters.
development.target: Primera inclusión en Chambers Latin America: Labour & Employment — Mexico.

matters.text:
DeForest advised a global automotive supplier on the labour integration following its acquisition of another automotive business. The firm designed and implemented a harmonised labour strategy across facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, covering employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.

The team also manages 35 active labour proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, aligning litigation strategy with the client’s unified post-acquisition governance model. Eduardo Garduño led the mandate.
matters.completion_status: Currently underway. The firm has implemented the labour integration strategy and manages 35 active labour proceedings.
decisive_source_quotes: The firm designed and implemented the labor integration strategy affecting facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labor governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.

Parallel to the integration, DeForest manages thirty-five active labor proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, ensuring that litigation strategy remains fully aligned with the client's unified post-acquisition governance model.

Lead Partner(s):
Eduardo Garduño.

matters.text:

The team designed and implemented the client’s negotiation and litigation strategy in union-representation proceedings while supporting operational continuity.

Through proactive dialogue and procedural management, the team prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads the mandate.
matters.completion_status: Ongoing. Work stoppages were prevented and escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism was avoided.
decisive_source_quotes: DeForest designed and implemented the client's negotiation and litigation strategy, guiding the company through complex union representation proceedings while preserving uninterrupted operations.

Through proactive dialogue and careful procedural management, the firm successfully prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response labor Mechanism, protecting both operational continuity and the client's long-term industrial stability.

matters.text:
DeForest represents an employer in wrongful-termination proceedings raising a procedural issue concerning recognition of its attorney-in-fact. The team challenged the labour court’s ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that legally recognised identity documentation had been improperly disregarded.

A Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s legal standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads the mandate.
matters.completion_status: Ongoing. A Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of legal standing and restored the client’s right to present its defence.
decisive_source_quotes: DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation.
The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

Lead Partner(s):
Javier Atzin Vallejo.

comparisons.tradeoff: TEKIA describe una exposición potencial mayor y estrategia de litigio constitucional, pero no documenta un resultado definitivo. REGSA es más acotado, pero aporta una capacidad colectiva no redundante y actividad ongoing expresamente indicada.

TEKIA añade litigación laboral y amparo, pero esa capacidad ya está mejor acreditada por Nueva Empresa, BADAK y Mextypsa.

comparisons.tradeoff: Ramsa tiene una gama preventiva más amplia, pero carece de un resultado concreto. Grupo Radio Centro documenta una investigación estructurada y prevención de litigio, aunque su escala económica no debe utilizarse por tratarse de un asunto confidencial.

Ramsa acredita auditorías, terminaciones sensibles y due diligence, pero se superpone con Art Human, SCOTCH y otros mandatos de compliance.

development.positioning: Plataforma laboral para empleadores con trabajo integrado en relaciones colectivas y prevención de huelgas, integración post-adquisición, reestructuraciones, litigios laborales de cartera, inspecciones y cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social.
development.hero_rationale: SCHAEFFLER es el mejor asunto hero porque demuestra, en un solo mandato, integración laboral post-adquisición, implementación multinivel en seis estados, armonización de documentación y relaciones colectivas para más de 5.000 empleados, y gestión paralela de 35 procedimientos activos. Frente al mandato de Volkswagen, que acredita una cartera relevante y gobernanza continua, SCHAEFFLER ofrece una transformación laboral definida y directamente atribuida a Eduardo Garduño.
development.target_rationale: El objetivo principal suministrado es primera inclusión. El objetivo secundario de subir múltiples bandas no es aplicable a una candidatura de primera inclusión y no debe presentarse como una posición actual ni como una previsión. La comprobación oficial acotada no encontró una coincidencia exacta de la firma en la tabla de Labour & Employment México, pero ello no acredita ausencia global de ranking. La investigación comparativa recuperada se limita a perfiles oficiales de tres firmas de Band 5 y permite contexto temático, no calibración completa del mercado.
development.principal_strength: La selección acredita una combinación poco uniforme de asuntos laborales patronales: integración post-adquisición de más de 5.000 empleados en seis estados, negociación colectiva y prevención de paros, litigios laborales de gran volumen, transiciones de plantilla, litigio constitucional laboral y cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social.
development.filing_recommendation: Presentar una candidatura de primera inclusión, con una narrativa empleador-side centrada en relaciones colectivas, integración de plantillas, carteras de litigios laborales y gobernanza laboral y de seguridad social. La evidencia permite una presentación sólida, pero la ventana de investigación debe confirmarse una sola vez para vincular expresamente los mandatos a ese período.
development.principal_vulnerability: La narrativa requiere confirmación única de actividad en la ventana de investigación. Además, la prueba de liderazgo individual se concentra en Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez; para los demás abogados suministrados no hay mandatos core con atribución personal suficiente.
