editorial_development.c2:
DeForest requests consideration for coverage in Labour & Employment in Mexico. The practice presents an employer-side offering that combines collective labour strategy, workforce integration, labour litigation, employment governance and labour and social-security compliance.

Representative work includes a post-acquisition labour integration affecting more than 5,000 employees across six states; collective labour mandates in which the team prevented work stoppages and addressed union-representation disputes; nationwide labour litigation management involving approximately 200 active proceedings; and workforce restructurings involving employer substitution, specialised-services structures and multi-company transitions. The team also handles inspections, internal employment investigations, constitutional labour litigation and preventive governance for industrial, infrastructure, consumer-facing and regulated businesses.

The practice’s leadership is demonstrated through named partners leading these mandates, while associates contribute to complex restructuring, REPSE and litigation work. This combination of collective labour capability, contentious experience and practical workforce-governance work supports appropriate Chambers coverage for the Mexico Labour & Employment market.
editorial_development.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on workforce stability, collective labour relations, employment litigation, labour and social-security compliance, inspections and workforce governance across Mexico. The team combines contentious and non-contentious work for employers operating in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including manufacturing, automotive, energy, infrastructure, technology, consumer services and financial services.

The practice is particularly active where employment strategy is closely connected to operational continuity. Its work includes post-acquisition labour integration, collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, prevention of work stoppages, nationwide labour litigation portfolios, workforce restructurings, employer substitutions, specialised-services compliance, internal investigations, employment documentation and social-security matters.

The team has advised on the harmonisation of labour structures for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees across six Mexican states following an acquisition; collective labour disputes involving union representation and strike risk; nationwide litigation platforms comprising approximately 200 active proceedings; and employment-governance projects for industrial workforces of up to approximately 17,000 employees. It also advises on labour-reform implementation, REPSE-related reviews and supplier audits, labour and social-security inspections, and constitutional labour litigation.

Eduardo Garduño leads the practice, with Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante, José Alberto Díaz Méndez and other members of the team contributing across collective labour, workforce governance, litigation, compliance and social-security mandates. The practice is positioned to support employers throughout the employment lifecycle, from preventive governance and documentation to high-risk collective disputes and complex contentious matters.
editorial_development.target: Primera inclusión en Chambers Latin America: Labour & Employment — Mexico.

matters.text:
DeForest advised a global automotive supplier on the labour integration following its acquisition of another automotive business. The firm designed and implemented a harmonised labour strategy across facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, covering employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.

The team also manages 35 active labour proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, aligning litigation strategy with the client’s unified post-acquisition governance model. Eduardo Garduño led the mandate.
matters.completion_status: Currently underway. The firm has implemented the labour integration strategy and manages 35 active labour proceedings.

Parallel to the integration, DeForest manages thirty-five active labor proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, ensuring that litigation strategy remains fully aligned with the client's unified post-acquisition governance model.

Eduardo Garduño.

A Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s legal standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads the mandate.

candidates.submission_bio:
Javier Atzin Vallejo is a partner in DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice. He leads employer-side collective labour, workforce-governance and contentious employment mandates for industrial and infrastructure operations in Mexico. His work includes designing negotiation and litigation strategy in a collective bargaining agreement ownership dispute, where the team prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism.

He also leads labour-governance work for energy infrastructure projects, including workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute prevention and workforce demobilisation. In contentious matters, he has led constitutional amparo proceedings that restored an employer’s right to present its defence and has combined constitutional litigation, procedural strategy and settlement negotiations to reduce a principal wrongful-termination claim materially. His practice brings together collective labour strategy, labour litigation and operational workforce governance.

editorial_development.positioning: Plataforma laboral para empleadores con trabajo integrado en relaciones colectivas y prevención de huelgas, integración post-adquisición, reestructuraciones, litigios laborales de cartera, inspecciones y cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social.
editorial_development.hero_rationale: SCHAEFFLER es el mejor asunto hero porque demuestra, en un solo mandato, integración laboral post-adquisición, implementación multinivel en seis estados, armonización de documentación y relaciones colectivas para más de 5.000 empleados, y gestión paralela de 35 procedimientos activos. Frente al mandato de Volkswagen, que acredita una cartera relevante y gobernanza continua, SCHAEFFLER ofrece una transformación laboral definida y directamente atribuida a Eduardo Garduño.
editorial_development.target_rationale: El objetivo principal suministrado es primera inclusión. El objetivo secundario de subir múltiples bandas no es aplicable a una candidatura de primera inclusión y no debe presentarse como una posición actual ni como una previsión. La comprobación oficial acotada no encontró una coincidencia exacta de la firma en la tabla de Labour & Employment México, pero ello no acredita ausencia global de ranking. La investigación comparativa recuperada se limita a perfiles oficiales de tres firmas de Band 5 y permite contexto temático, no calibración completa del mercado.
editorial_development.principal_strength: La selección acredita una combinación poco uniforme de asuntos laborales patronales: integración post-adquisición de más de 5.000 empleados en seis estados, negociación colectiva y prevención de paros, litigios laborales de gran volumen, transiciones de plantilla, litigio constitucional laboral y cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social.
editorial_development.filing_recommendation: Presentar una candidatura de primera inclusión, con una narrativa empleador-side centrada en relaciones colectivas, integración de plantillas, carteras de litigios laborales y gobernanza laboral y de seguridad social. La evidencia permite una presentación sólida, pero la ventana de investigación debe confirmarse una sola vez para vincular expresamente los mandatos a ese período.
editorial_development.principal_vulnerability: La narrativa requiere confirmación única de actividad en la ventana de investigación. Además, la prueba de liderazgo individual se concentra en Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez; para los demás abogados suministrados no hay mandatos core con atribución personal suficiente.

El Audit renderizado lo corrige y advierte que Benteler no debe sostener la candidatura de Jaime, pero la estructura de desarrollo sigue siendo contradictoria. Elimine Benteler de los supporting_matters de Jaime o registre expresamente que no tiene función atribuida; no cambie la fuente ni pida reconfirmación.

acceptance.evidence: La mayor parte del documento preserva identidades, roles, estados y monedas, pero la ficha estratégica de Jaime Bustamante le asigna un papel de lead en Benteler que la fuente atribuye a Eduardo Garduño. El Audit renderizado corrige esa atribución, por lo que existe una divergencia interna que debe repararse.

SCHAEFFLER, Brose, GeNI, BADAK, Grupo Solana y Nueva Empresa conservan resultados, escala y liderazgo relevantes. Sin embargo, Bonatti pierde la conciliación de la mayoría de más de veinte controversias y la reducción aproximada del 80% de exposición; además, varios asuntos de sección E pierden exposiciones económicas documentadas.

SCOTCH es el único asunto presentado en D y tiene publish_status=publishable con confidentialityConfirmed=true. Los demás asuntos seleccionados aparecen en E. B9, B10 y C2 utilizan descripciones anónimas de asuntos restringidos y no revelan sus clientes; no se publica el valor expresamente confidencial de Omron.

El Audit desarrolla categorías, razones, asuntos, roles, evidencia externa, brechas y acciones para los ocho abogados, y corrige correctamente la categoría incompatible de Javier Atzin Vallejo. No obstante, la estructura de desarrollo de Jaime Bustamante contiene una atribución personal falsa respecto de Benteler, lo que impide considerar coherente toda la estrategia individual.

B9 desarrolla casos personales sustantivos para Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez, con mandatos y contribuciones concretas. José se mantiene como Associate y se presenta como lead lawyer, no como socio. Los perfiles sin prueba suficiente se describen de forma prudente y sin inventar liderazgo.

C2 contiene un argumento de cobertura fundamentado en integración post-adquisición de más de 5,000 empleados, prevención de paros, controversias sindicales, aproximadamente 200 procedimientos, sustituciones patronales, REPSE, inspecciones y litigio constitucional. No afirma una banda ni un ranking establecido.

Submission y Audit comparten el mismo hero, SCHAEFFLER, y la misma cartera de 20 asuntos: 19 confidenciales y SCOTCH como publicable. El Audit compara expresamente SCHAEFFLER con Volkswagen y explica reservas concretas como TEKIA frente a REGSA y Ramsa frente a Grupo Radio Centro, además de justificar Enerflex como reserva por su orientación employee-side.

El Audit ofrece un veredicto de primera inclusión, rechaza correctamente hablar de subida de bandas, explica las limitaciones de la comprobación oficial y del research comparativo, justifica el hero, enumera la cartera, analiza a cada candidato y establece acciones concretas. También mantiene la incertidumbre temporal como seguimiento interno y no como prueba de inelegibilidad.

letter.portfolio: Cartera recomendada, en orden estratégico: 1. SCHAEFFLER — hero: Eduardo Garduño lideró la integración post-adquisición de más de 5.000 empleados en seis estados, con armonización de contratos, convenios colectivos, reglamentos, comisiones mixtas y políticas, y 35 procedimientos activos. 2. Brose México: Javier Atzin Vallejo dirigió estrategia de negociación y litigio en controversia de representatividad sindical; la fuente atribuye prevención de paros y de escalamiento bajo el Mecanismo Laboral de Respuesta Rápida del T-MEC. 3. GeNI de México: Eduardo Garduño y Carlos Rivera lideraron negociación colectiva ante huelga inminente; la fuente atribuye prevención de la huelga y continuidad productiva. 4. Volkswagen de México y VW Financial Services: Eduardo Garduño lidera procedimientos activos y asesoría sobre contratos, reglamentos, disciplina, poderes y gobernanza. 5. Cinemex: Eduardo Garduño y Fernanda Priego codirigen aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos, conciliaciones, reestructuraciones y prevención; Erick Pérez integra el equipo. 6. Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge: José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable de una reestructuración de aproximadamente ocho compañías, entidad de servicios especializados, sustituciones patronales, transición de plantilla y litigio de seguridad social. 7. Coats de México: Eduardo Garduño lidera transformación multisede, documentación laboral y colectiva y negociaciones sindicales que, según la fuente, preservaron estabilidad operativa. 8. Bonatti SpA / Bonatti México: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera arquitectura laboral, prevención de controversias y desmovilización para infraestructura energética; la fuente atribuye prevención de huelga inminente. 9. Benteler: Eduardo Garduño lidera respuesta a controversia de representatividad sindical mediante litigio, estrategia colectiva y negociación con sindicatos competidores. 10. Mextypsa: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera estructuración contractual y de cumplimiento, desmovilización y amparo que reabrió el litigio; persisten más de 20 controversias. 11. Nueva Empresa: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera amparo en el que un Tribunal Colegiado concedió protección, reconoció legitimación y restituyó defensa. 12. BADAK: Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera litigio constitucional, estrategia procesal y negociación; la fuente informa reducción de aproximadamente MXN 1,06 millones a MXN 20.000. 13. Grupo Solana: José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable en sustitución patronal para más de 1.200 personas, con reactivación de registro patronal y transición sin interrupción. 14. letter.leadership:
La limitación común: la búsqueda individual oficial acotada no encontró coincidencias exactas en la tabla de Chambers Labour & Employment México; no demuestra ausencia de reconocimiento en otras prácticas o ediciones. Las categorías son objetivos de candidatura, no reconocimientos establecidos ni previsiones.

Eduardo Garduño — candidato individual principal, objetivo Band 5. Es socio y concentra la atribución más amplia: lidera SCHAEFFLER, GeNI, Volkswagen, Coats, REGSA, SEBNMX y Recicla Ambiente, y codirige Cinemex. La candidatura debe centrarse en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas de alto riesgo, litigación de cartera y gobernanza industrial. El objetivo Band 5 se conserva por seniority y reiteración de liderazgo, sin afirmar ranking actual. Deben obtenerse referencias sobre liderazgo, negociación y servicio continuado.

Javier Atzin Vallejo — segundo candidato individual, objetivo Band 5. Es socio; por ello, la sugerencia previa de Associate to Watch se sustituyó correctamente por una candidatura de socio. Su prueba diferenciada comprende Brose, Bonatti, Mextypsa, Nueva Empresa, BADAK y Bosch. Debe posicionarse en relaciones colectivas, prevención de paros, litigación constitucional laboral, proyectos industriales y seguridad social. Faltan referencias y confirmación de actividad dentro de la ventana aplicable.

Jaime Bustamante — candidato de apoyo, objetivo Band 5. Es socio y lidera Art Human y Grupo Radio Centro, con evidencia de compliance preventivo, inspecciones, investigaciones internas y gestión de riesgo. Puede presentarse, pero su caso individual es menos fuerte en relaciones colectivas que los dos candidatos principales. Benteler y Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge no deben usarse como prueba de su liderazgo: las fuentes atribuyen esos mandatos a Eduardo Garduño y José Alberto Díaz Méndez, respectivamente. Requiere más referencias y mandatos core personalmente atribuidos.

José Alberto Díaz Méndez — candidato Associate to Watch. Su rol confirmado es Associate; debe describirse como associate lead o responsable, nunca como socio aunque el campo fuente diga “Lead Partner(s)”. Sus mandatos sustantivos son SCOTCH, Grupo Solana y Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge, además de participación de equipo en Volkswagen y Bosch. La categoría es congruente con trabajo en REPSE, sustitución patronal, transición de plantilla y seguridad social. Debe documentarse su función técnica concreta y obtener referencias de clientes.

Erick Pérez — desarrollar, sin candidatura formal. Es Associate y figura como integrante del equipo en Volkswagen, Cinemex y Benteler, pero no se le atribuyen dirección de audiencia, estrategia, negociación ni responsabilidad autónoma. Una eventual candidatura Associate to Watch exige roles personales repetidos y verificables.

Andrés Cabrera — desarrollar. Es Associate; la bio menciona trabajo contencioso, pero no hay asunto core atribuido. No procede candidatura hasta contar con dos o tres mandatos relevantes que identifiquen función, etapa procesal o resultado.

Raymundo Carreño — desarrollar. Es Associate. La experiencia previa puede reforzar su bio, pero no sustituye trabajo actual personalmente atribuido. No tiene mandatos core a su nombre; una candidatura Associate to Watch requiere evidencia contemporánea.

Edgar Barreto — desarrollar. Es Associate y su perfil es coherente con litigación laboral e IMSS, pero no hay mandatos core ni resultados atribuidos. Debe permanecer visible como integrante del equipo, sin candidatura individual en esta edición.

letter.evidence_gaps: Reservas y exclusiones comparativas: American Axle & Manufacturing queda en reserva por discrepancia entre “American Axle Manufactury” y “American Axle & Manufacturing”, inicio a comienzos de 2026 y falta de resultado final; no debe fijarse una variante como definitiva. TEKIA acredita estrategia de litigio y amparo, pero no resultado definitivo; queda detrás de Nueva Empresa, BADAK y Mextypsa, que aportan resultados procesales o cuantificados. Ramsa aporta auditorías, terminaciones sensibles y due diligence, pero se superpone con Art Human y SCOTCH; Grupo Radio Centro añade investigación interna y prevención de controversias. Securitas y Natividad Abogados muestran volumen, pero menos detalle jurídico que Cinemex, Volkswagen y los asuntos colectivos del núcleo. Omron, SKF, AUNDE, Sirushi/Shirushi, Corrugados y Empaques de Oriente y SEBNMX son asesoría o gobernanza útil, pero generalmente menos diferenciadora; en Sirushi/Shirushi persiste discrepancia de nombre. Enerflex es trabajo directo de controversias, pero el cliente fue el empleado y se reserva para mantener una narrativa employer-side. Grupo Dos describe una negociación exitosa, pero carece del detalle jurídico, procesal y cuantitativo de los asuntos seleccionados. La falta de fechas exactas o de estado formal no demuestra inelegibilidad; los asuntos con actividad narrativa pueden describirse como en curso, sin inferir fechas, cierres o resultados definitivos.
letter.executive_assessment: Veredicto ejecutivo: presentar una candidatura de primera inclusión en Chambers Latin America: Labour & Employment — Mexico; no procede hablar de subida de bandas. La comprobación oficial acotada no halló una coincidencia exacta de DeForest en la tabla de Labour & Employment México, sin acreditar ausencia de reconocimiento en otros alcances ni permitir prever una banda. La propuesta muestra una práctica employer-side coherente en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas, prevención de paros, litigación de cartera, reestructuraciones, cumplimiento laboral y seguridad social. SCHAEFFLER es el hero: frente a Volkswagen, que acredita cartera y gobernanza continuada, combina una integración definida tras adquisición, armonización laboral y colectiva en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, 35 procedimientos activos y liderazgo atribuido a Eduardo Garduño. Tres perfiles oficiales recuperados de Band 5 muestran como contexto capacidades de negociación colectiva, litigios individuales y colectivos, seguridad social y asesoría no contenciosa, pero no aportan calibración completa ni posición comparativa. La vulnerabilidad pendiente es confirmar una sola vez que los asuntos seleccionados reflejan actividad relevante en la ventana de investigación; la evidencia individual se concentra en Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez.

editorial_previous_drafts.c2:
DeForest respectfully requests consideration for coverage in Labour & Employment, Mexico. The practice acts for employers on complex workforce matters in which collective labour relations, litigation, social security, compliance and business continuity intersect.

Its representative work includes post-acquisition labour integration across six states for more than 5,000 employees; strategic collective bargaining and union-representation disputes in manufacturing and energy infrastructure; nationwide employment-litigation portfolios involving approximately 200 active proceedings; and multi-company restructurings involving specialised-services entities, employer substitutions and workforce transitions. The team also advises employers on employment documentation, workplace regulations, inspections, labour policies, conciliation, constitutional employment litigation and social security structures.

The practice is led by Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo and Jaime Bustamante, with José Alberto Díaz Méndez contributing leadership on REPSE, employer-substitution and restructuring mandates. Together, the team offers an integrated employer-side capability across collective labour strategy, contentious employment work and preventive workforce governance for businesses operating in regulated and labour-intensive sectors.
editorial_previous_drafts.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on matters where workforce stability, regulatory compliance and operational continuity are closely connected. The team combines labour advisory, collective labour relations, employment litigation, social security, workplace compliance and workforce governance for domestic and multinational businesses operating throughout Mexico.

The practice is active in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including automotive manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, technology, telecommunications, financial services and consumer-facing operations. Its work spans the employment lifecycle, from employment documentation, workplace regulations, labour policies and inspections to collective bargaining, union-representation disputes, workforce restructurings, REPSE compliance, employer substitutions, social security matters and litigation.

Representative work includes post-acquisition labour integration across six Mexican states for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees; collective bargaining and union-representation matters in which the team prevented threatened work stoppages; nationwide employment-litigation portfolios involving hundreds of active proceedings; and multi-company restructurings involving specialised-services entities, workforce transitions and social security litigation.

Eduardo Garduño leads complex workforce integration, collective labour and employment-litigation mandates. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads work involving industrial relations, social security, strategic infrastructure projects and constitutional employment litigation. Jaime Bustamante advises on workforce strategy, employment disputes, compliance and employment-risk management. José Alberto Díaz Méndez leads mandates involving REPSE, employer substitutions, labour restructuring and social security matters.

The team’s approach integrates contentious and preventive work: managing active disputes while strengthening the documentation, labour-governance and collective-relations frameworks that support employers’ ongoing operations.

matters.text:
DeForest acts for an engineering and infrastructure business on labour governance for major projects, with Javier Atzin Vallejo identified as Lead Partner. The work includes the Guadalajara Metro Line 4 Project, a USD 552 million development requiring project-based recruitment, documentation, workforce administration and eventual demobilisation, as well as litigation arising from a wind-farm project.

The team designed contractual and compliance architecture for the metro project and supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies. In the wind-farm dispute, it successfully challenged an adverse labour judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the employer’s procedural rights and reopening the litigation. DeForest currently manages more than 20 labour disputes for the employer, representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million.

DeForest advises an energy-infrastructure contractor on labour governance for major projects, including the Energía Mayakan Pipeline Expansion, valued at more than USD 2 billion, and the Cuxtal II expansion, valued at USD 2.5 billion. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The ongoing mandate includes workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute-prevention strategies and workforce demobilisation.

Alongside this preventive work, the team managed more than 20 labour disputes arising during project execution, resolving the overwhelming majority through conciliation and reducing potential financial exposure by approximately 80%. DeForest also prevented an imminent strike that threatened to halt operations linked to strategic energy infrastructure.

Following a global acquisition, DeForest was appointed to lead the post-acquisition labour integration of an automotive supplier’s Mexican manufacturing operations. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner. The mandate covered facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua and required harmonisation of employment structures while operations continued.

The team designed and implemented a labour integration strategy for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies. In parallel, DeForest manages 35 active labour proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, aligning litigation strategy with the employer’s unified post-acquisition governance model.

DeForest advises an automotive supplier in an ongoing collective bargaining matter arising from a deteriorating union relationship and an imminent strike risk. Eduardo Garduño and Carlos Rivera are identified as Lead Partners. The threatened disruption had the potential to affect production across multiple automotive supply chains.

The firm led collective bargaining negotiations, rebuilding dialogue between management and union representatives and designing a renewed agreement that balanced operational efficiency with employee expectations. The negotiations prevented the strike and introduced process improvements and operational efficiencies while uninterrupted production was preserved.

DeForest represents a private-sector employer in two ongoing wrongful-termination proceedings. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matters arose after a labour court refused to recognise the company’s attorney-in-fact, disregarded the employer’s defence and issued an adverse ruling despite notarial documentation concerning the attorney’s legal identity.

The team challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the court’s approach violated due process and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. The source describes financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million.

DeForest represents a manufacturing employer in an ongoing collective labour dispute concerning ownership of a collective bargaining agreement at a facility in Querétaro. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matter arose amid union-representation challenges under Mexico’s changing collective labour framework, with direct business-continuity implications for the operation.

The team designed and implemented the employer’s negotiation and litigation strategy, combining proactive dialogue with procedural management in the representation proceedings. DeForest prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism while preserving uninterrupted operations.

DeForest advises a private-security employer on employment litigation and preventive workforce governance as the business expands across Puebla, Mexico City, Torreón and Veracruz. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with Maximiliano Hernández and Erick Pérez listed as team members. The employer operates a dispersed workforce and faces ongoing employment and regulatory exposure.

The firm manages more than 50 labour proceedings with aggregate exposure approaching MXN 10 million. Alongside the litigation portfolio, DeForest advises on documentation, employment governance and risk mitigation, applying a coordinated strategy across the employer’s multi-jurisdictional operations.

DeForest acts for an engineering and technology business on an ongoing portfolio of legacy employment litigation involving potential exposure approaching MXN 16 million. Jaime Bustamante is identified as Lead Partner. The mandate includes negotiations relating to two adverse labour judgments valued at approximately MXN 6.5 million and a constitutional amparo challenging the reasoning underlying one of the labour decisions.

The firm designed a coordinated strategy combining litigation, constitutional review and commercial negotiation to contain overall financial risk. The constitutional amparo remains ongoing.

DeForest represents a technology consultancy in several employment disputes involving wrongful-termination claims with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 1.5 million. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. One principal claim had escalated to approximately MXN 1.06 million when constitutional relief became available.

The team combined constitutional litigation, procedural strategy and commercial negotiation. Through sequencing of legal actions and settlement discussions, DeForest reduced the principal claim from approximately MXN 1.06 million to MXN 20,000, representing a reduction of approximately 98%, while continuing to manage the remaining proceedings.

DeForest continues to advise a major industrial employer and its financial-services affiliate on labour governance for their Mexican operations. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez, Ana Ruiz and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members. The ongoing mandate combines contentious and preventive employment work for operations in Puebla.

The firm manages active labour proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 280 million. It also advises on employment agreements, internal workplace regulations, disciplinary procedures, corporate powers of attorney and broader workforce-governance initiatives, integrating dispute management with preventive labour strategy.

DeForest advises an industrial employer with approximately 17,000 people across multiple business divisions on employment and labour governance. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner, and José Alberto Díaz is listed as a team member. The ongoing mandate addresses governance for a large industrial workforce.

The team advises on employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labour-governance policies and union-related matters. It also leads employer-registration processes for a group company and coordinates social security structures across the organisation.

DeForest advises a manufacturer on an ongoing workforce transformation affecting facilities in Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz and Maximiliano Hernández listed as team members. The mandate combines redesign of the employment framework with sensitive collective labour issues relevant to manufacturing continuity.

The firm developed the employer’s labour architecture, including employment agreements, labour policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce-governance protocols. It also negotiated union-related matters involving exposure exceeding MXN 12.5 million and led collective bargaining discussions that enabled the employer to preserve operational stability during the restructuring.

DeForest advises an industrial employer on the design of its labour-governance framework and on union-representativeness proceedings. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with Ana Ruíz listed as a team member. The mandate combines preventive employment structures with collective labour representation in Mexico’s post-reform environment.

The firm designed employment documentation, labour policies and a collective bargaining framework, while leading union-representativeness proceedings requiring procedural strategy and continuing engagement with labour authorities.

DeForest represents an automotive supplier in a union-representativeness dispute affecting a manufacturing facility in Puebla. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members. The matter concerns a collective labour dispute capable of disrupting operations.

The firm assumed responsibility for the employer’s strategic response, combining litigation, collective bargaining strategy and continuing negotiations with competing unions. Alongside the representation proceedings, the team is implementing employment agreements, internal labour policies and collective bargaining documentation to reinforce the employer’s labour-governance platform.

DeForest acts for a nationwide cinema operator with more than 11,000 employees on an ongoing employment-litigation and labour-governance mandate. Eduardo Garduño and Fernanda Priego are identified as Lead Partners, with Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members.

The firm coordinates a nationwide litigation platform comprising approximately 200 active labour proceedings with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 60.5 million. Its work includes conciliation proceedings, workforce restructurings, employment documentation and preventive governance measures intended to reduce future labour contingencies across the employer’s multi-jurisdictional workforce.

DeForest advises an employer operating approximately 700 employees across multiple Mexican states on labour governance and collective labour strategy. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner. The workforce is geographically dispersed and the mandate involves negotiations with multiple unions.

The team advises on labour, collective bargaining and union negotiations in Puebla, Querétaro, Silao, Aguascalientes, Ramos Arizpe and Apodaca. It coordinates employment strategy across these jurisdictions while addressing local operational requirements and different union relationships.

DeForest advised SCOTCH on restructuring its corporate and labour framework following the introduction of Mexico’s specialised-services regime. José Alberto Díaz Méndez is identified as Lead Partner. The multidisciplinary mandate required alignment of the business model with the evolving outsourcing and REPSE framework.

Working across its corporate and labour practices, DeForest reviewed the client’s corporate structure, specialised-services model, bylaws and REPSE registration. The team also audited more than 80 suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised-services agreements.

DeForest advised a diversified automotive and real estate group employing more than 1,200 people on an employer-substitution process affecting its workforce structure. José Alberto Díaz Méndez is identified as Lead Partner. The project required coordination with labour and regulatory authorities after the group’s employer registration had been cancelled.

The team designed and executed the legal strategy to reactivate the employer registration, enabling the employer-substitution process to proceed without disrupting operations. DeForest coordinated the labour transition and addressed compliance with the applicable employment framework while preserving workforce stability during the restructuring.

José Alberto Díaz Méndez is identified as Lead Partner for DeForest’s labour restructuring mandate for a manufacturing group. The project affects approximately eight companies operating across multiple Mexican states and involves separation of business functions, redesign of the group’s employment model and development of a specialised-services platform under Mexico’s post-outsourcing framework.

DeForest developed the legal strategy for creation of a specialised-services entity, employer-substitution processes, redesign of corporate purposes and a workforce transition across the operating companies. The firm also represents the employer in social security litigation before the Federal Court of Administrative Justice challenging tax assessments relating to two manufacturing facilities.

The firm led collective bargaining negotiations, rebuilding dialogue between management and union representatives and designing a renewed agreement that balanced operational efficiency with employee expectations. The team challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the court’s approach violated due process and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. The confirmed matter value is approximately USD 171,494.21; the narrative separately describes financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million.

Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matter arose amid union-representation challenges under Mexico’s evolving collective labour framework.

Representative work includes a post-acquisition labour integration affecting more than 5,000 employees across six states; collective labour mandates in which the team prevented work stoppages and addressed union-representation disputes; nationwide labour litigation management involving approximately 200 active proceedings; and workforce restructurings involving employer substitution, specialised-services structures and multi-company transitions. The team also handles inspections, internal employment investigations, constitutional labour litigation and preventive governance for industrial, infrastructure, consumer-facing and regulated businesses.

The practice’s leadership is demonstrated through named partners leading these mandates, while associates contribute to complex restructuring, REPSE and litigation work. This combination of collective labour capability, contentious experience and practical workforce-governance work supports appropriate Chambers coverage for the Mexico Labour & Employment market.
editorial_previous_drafts.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on workforce stability, collective labour relations, employment litigation, labour and social-security compliance, inspections and workforce governance across Mexico. The team combines contentious and non-contentious work for employers operating in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including manufacturing, automotive, energy, infrastructure, technology, consumer services and financial services.

The practice is particularly active where employment strategy is closely connected to operational continuity. Its work includes post-acquisition labour integration, collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, prevention of work stoppages, nationwide labour litigation portfolios, workforce restructurings, employer substitutions, specialised-services compliance, internal investigations, employment documentation and social-security matters.

The team has advised on the harmonisation of labour structures for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees across six Mexican states following an acquisition; collective labour disputes involving union representation and strike risk; nationwide litigation platforms comprising approximately 200 active proceedings; and employment-governance projects for industrial workforces of up to approximately 17,000 employees. It also advises on labour-reform implementation, REPSE-related reviews and supplier audits, labour and social-security inspections, and constitutional labour litigation.

Eduardo Garduño leads the practice, with Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante, José Alberto Díaz Méndez and other members of the team contributing across collective labour, workforce governance, litigation, compliance and social-security mandates. The practice is positioned to support employers throughout the employment lifecycle, from preventive governance and documentation to high-risk collective disputes and complex contentious matters.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 5
matters.rawNotes:
Nueva Empresa, S.C. engaged DeForest in two high-value wrongful termination proceedings that raised issues extending well beyond financial exposure. Following procedural objections concerning the legal standing of the company's attorney-in-fact, the labor court refused to recognise the company's representation, disregarded its defence and issued an adverse ruling despite the existence of valid notarial documentation confirming the attorney's legal identity.

The dispute presented a significant constitutional question concerning due process, legal certainty and the recognition of legally valid identity changes, creating an important opportunity to clarify procedural standards within Mexico's labor justice system.

DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

Beyond the financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million, the matter is significant for reinforcing constitutional protections governing procedural fairness and the legal recognition of identity, establishing an important precedent with broader implications for labor litigation in Mexico.

Through disciplined sequencing of legal actions and settlement discussions, the firm reduced one of the principal claims from approximately MXN 1.06 million to MXN 20,000, representing a reduction of approximately 98% while continuing to manage the remaining proceedings.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to contain significant employment liabilities through sophisticated litigation strategy while preserving business continuity for rapidly growing technology companies.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 20
matters.rawNotes:
Benteler, one of the world's leading automotive suppliers, entrusted DeForest with one of the most sensitive labor challenges currently affecting industrial employers in Mexico: a union representativeness dispute capable of disrupting operations at one of its manufacturing facilities in Puebla. The matter arose within the broader transformation of Mexico's collective labor framework, where representation challenges increasingly influence business continuity across the automotive sector.

DeForest assumed responsibility for the client's strategic response, combining litigation, collective bargaining strategy and continuous negotiations with the competing unions. The firm's objective extended beyond resolving the legal dispute; it focused on preserving operational stability while ensuring full compliance with Mexico's labor legislation and respect for employees' collective rights.

Alongside the representation proceedings, DeForest continues strengthening the client's labor governance platform through the implementation of employment agreements, internal labor policies and collective bargaining documentation, reinforcing long-term organisational stability.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 6
matters.rawNotes:
Brose México entrusted DeForest with the management of a highly sensitive collective labor dispute involving the ownership of the collective bargaining agreement at one of its manufacturing facilities in Querétaro. The proceedings formed part of the broader transformation of Mexico's collective labor relations framework, where union representation challenges increasingly affect business continuity for major industrial employers.

DeForest designed and implemented the client's negotiation and litigation strategy, guiding the company through complex union representation proceedings while preserving uninterrupted operations. Through proactive dialogue and careful procedural management, the firm successfully prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response labor Mechanism, protecting both operational continuity and the client's long-term industrial stability.

The matter demonstrates DeForest's ability to navigate one of the most challenging aspects of Mexico's post-reform labor landscape, combining collective bargaining expertise with strategic business risk management.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 7
matters.rawNotes:
One of Mexico's most extraordinary labor disputes gave rise to this engagement. A former senior executive obtained a labor judgment exceeding MXN 2.162 billion, exposing Enerflex and indirectly PEMEX to unprecedented financial and governance risks. Against this exceptional backdrop, the employee retained DeForest to develop an alternative strategy capable of unlocking negotiations that had reached complete deadlock.

Rather than relying exclusively on litigation, DeForest designed a parallel mediation strategy running alongside the judicial proceedings. The firm established common valuation criteria, governance-based negotiation parameters and structured settlement mechanisms capable of facilitating constructive dialogue between parties that had previously been unwilling to negotiate.

The strategy ultimately generated a series of favourable settlement agreements that preserved the employee's legitimate interests while significantly reducing systemic exposure for Enerflex and preventing PEMEX from facing joint liability arising from one of the largest labor awards ever issued in Mexico. The matter remains ongoing, with DeForest continuing to coordinate negotiations alongside PEMEX's in-house legal team.

This engagement reflects the firm's ability to resolve disputes where legal complexity, commercial interests and public-sector exposure intersect at the highest level.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 22
matters.rawNotes:
Cinemex, one of Mexico's largest cinema operators with more than 11,000 employees nationwide, relies on DeForest to manage one of the country's most significant labor litigation portfolios following the operational disruption generated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The client's nationwide footprint requires a unified legal strategy capable of maintaining consistency across multiple jurisdictions operating under evolving labor reform criteria.

DeForest coordinates a nationwide litigation platform comprising approximately two hundred active labor proceedings with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 60.5 million. Beyond litigation management, the team leads conciliation proceedings, advises on workforce restructurings, strengthens employment documentation and continuously refines preventive governance measures designed to reduce future labor contingencies.

By combining centralised litigation management with preventive advisory, the firm enables the client to maintain operational stability while reducing systemic employment risk across one of Mexico's largest consumer-facing workforces.

Eduardo Garduño and Fernanda Priego lead the mandate, with Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos identified as team members.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 12
matters.rawNotes:
Grupo DOS, a technology company specialising in advanced hardware and software solutions, retained DeForest to resolve a complex labor dispute carrying significant financial and operational implications. Beyond the immediate litigation, the client sought a long-term employment strategy capable of supporting the continued growth of its business.

DeForest successfully negotiated the resolution of the dispute, substantially reducing the client's legal and reputational exposure while creating the foundation for an ongoing strategic relationship. Following the successful outcome, the parties entered discussions for a long-term retainer under which DeForest would become the company's external labor counsel across the full spectrum of employment matters.

The engagement reflects how successful dispute resolution can evolve into trusted long-term strategic partnerships based on business-oriented legal advice.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 16
matters.rawNotes:
Robert Bosch de México operates one of the country's largest industrial workforces, employing approximately 17,000 people across multiple business divisions. Maintaining consistent labor governance within an organisation of this scale requires sophisticated employment structures capable of supporting operational efficiency while ensuring full regulatory compliance.

DeForest advises the client on the design and implementation of employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labor governance policies and union-related matters, while also leading employer registration processes for Bosch Rexroth and coordinating social security structures across the organisation.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to build and maintain labor governance platforms supporting complex industrial operations where workforce management directly influences operational continuity and long-term business performance.
matters.optimizedText:

The mandate covers employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labour-governance policies and union-related matters, together with employer-registration processes and coordination of social-security structures.

Javier Atzin Vallejo leads the work, supported by José Alberto Díaz.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 17
matters.rawNotes:
Coats de México engaged DeForest to support a significant workforce transformation affecting multiple manufacturing facilities across Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. The mandate required not only the redesign of the client's employment framework but also the careful management of sensitive collective labor issues capable of affecting manufacturing continuity.

The firm developed the client's labor architecture from the ground up, including employment agreements, labor policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce governance protocols. Simultaneously, DeForest negotiated union-related matters involving exposure exceeding MXN 12.5 million while leading collective bargaining discussions that enabled the client to preserve operational stability throughout the restructuring process.

The engagement highlights the firm's ability to combine workforce transformation with sophisticated collective labor negotiations for major industrial employers.

The firm developed employment agreements, labour policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce-governance protocols, while negotiating union-related matters and leading collective bargaining discussions.

The collective bargaining work enabled the client to preserve operational stability during the restructuring. Eduardo Garduño leads the mandate, supported by José Alberto Díaz and Maximiliano Hernández.
